problem: Existing 3D-aware object-goal navigation agents need high-dimensional 3D scene representations that must be learned, which incurs large training costs. Zero-shot methods usually rely on 2D VLM-based semantic maps that lack fine-grained spatial understanding.
motivation: Fine-grained 3D spatial understanding can improve object goal navigation, but training 3D-aware agents is expensive. The paper's observation is that pre-trained 3D VLMs already encode point clouds and text into a shared semantic-geometric space, so this capability can be used without any training.
key_idea: Use a pre-trained 3D vision-language model to embed environment point clouds and the goal text into one space, build a language-conditioned 3D potential map from them, and combine it with a cost-utility exploration method for zero-shot object goal navigation.
insight: Abstract only: the claimed reason it works is that a pre-trained 3D VLM provides joint physical-semantic reasoning, so no training is needed. The abstract also says PLM works as an adapter with various 3D VLMs, which suggests the gain comes from the map-and-planning framework and not from one specific model. No ablation details are available.
method: 3D VLM encoding: a pre-trained 3D vision-language model encodes environmental point clouds and textual instructions into a unified semantic-geometric space.
Language-conditioned 3D potential map: the point-language similarity is used to build a 3D potential map for the goal.
Cost-utility exploration: the potential map is combined with a cost-utility method to choose exploration targets efficiently in a zero-shot way.
Adapter-style design: the framework is compatible with various 3D VLMs.

results: On three mainstream datasets, PLM improves success rate over baselines, with gains of 2.0%~29.6% on HM3D. It is competitive in navigation efficiency with the best-performing method and works with various 3D VLMs. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the specific numbers and setup are unknown.
Performance likely depends on the quality of the pre-trained 3D VLM and on point cloud reconstruction, and the abstract says only 'competitive' efficiency.
